mechanism_narrative: The observed decline in PARKS mobility, indicative of colder weather and the onset of winter, will continue to reduce outdoor activities and subsequently depress retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, despite PARKS mobility continuing its downward trend or remaining below baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained week-on-week increase in WORKPLACES mobility, as observed in the last two weeks, signals a gradual return to office routines, which will drive a modest increase in retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES increases week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the last 28 days, even if WORKPLACES mobility continues to rise for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in TRANSIT station mobility by more than one percentage point week-on-week indicates a broader increase in out-of-home movement, which will lead to a short-term boost in retail and recreation activity over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not increase relative to the prior 14 days, despite TRANSIT mobility rising by more than 1 point week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: The persistently elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility, remaining above 7% from baseline, suggests a continued preference for staying home, which will suppress any significant recovery in retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is significantly higher than the last 28 days, while RESIDENTIAL mobility remains consistently above 7%.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous decline in PARKS mobility below baseline and a week-on-week fall in TRANSIT usage indicates a broad reduction in discretionary outdoor and public movement, leading to a further decrease in retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below 0 AND TRANSIT falls week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days increases relative to the last 28 days, despite PARKS falling below 0 and TRANSIT declining week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent stability of GROCERY_PHARM mobility within a narrow range (e.g., +/- 1 point) over the last three weeks suggests a lack of new drivers for out-of-home activity, implying retail and recreation will remain stagnant or slightly decline over the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains within +/- 1 point for 3 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days shows a significant increase, despite GROCERY_PHARM mobility remaining stable within +/- 1 point for three consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Even if WORKPLACES mobility shows a week-on-week increase, the persistent high level of RESIDENTIAL mobility (above 7%) indicates a strong hybrid work preference, which will temper the potential positive impact on retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES increases week-on-week AND RESIDENTIAL remains above 7%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days shows a significant increase, despite WORKPLACES rising week-on-week and RESIDENTIAL remaining above 7%.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained negative baseline for RETAIL_REC, consistently around -20% over the last four weeks, indicates a persistent underlying suppression of discretionary activity, suggesting this stagnation will continue over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days shows a significant positive shift, breaking the established pattern of stagnation around -20%.
